metadata.title: Teacher and school stress profiles: A multilevel examination and associations with work-related outcomes

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2018 data from a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design and applies TALIS-provided teacher weights (TCHWGT) and school weights (SCHWGT) to account for selection and participation probabilities at different sampling stages. To reflect the nested structure of teachers within schools, the authors also specify complex survey handling in Mplus using the “type = complex” option. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty is handled via the Mplus complex-sampling framework rather than explicit replicate variance estimation. Because the analysis is person-centered (latent profile analysis) rather than predictive ML, the paper’s weighting strategy is focused on producing population-representative parameter estimates for profile membership and outcome comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are non-PV latent/scale outcomes (teacher strain and occupational commitment) and profile indicators from TALIS questionnaires, not cognitive achievement scores with PVs. Missing data handling is reported as full information maximum likelihood (FIML) in Mplus, which is treated here as multiple imputation under the schema mapping. The paper provides missingness rates for teacher-level and school-level variables, supporting that missing-data treatment was implemented rather than omitted.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Phase one uses TALIS 2018 Australian teachers: 3117 teachers from 225 schools. The study excludes 456 teachers and 8 schools from the original TALIS 2018 sample because they had missing data on all substantive variables and/or substantial missing data at the school level. Participants are teachers teaching ISCED Level 2 (lower secondary). The analysis uses teacher-level substantive variables (workload stress, student behavior stress, expectation stress; strain; occupational commitment) and school-level substantive variables (school-average strain and occupational commitment), with missing data handled via FIML; missingness is reported as ~11% for substantive teacher-level variables and 0% for school-level substantive variables.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 Australian teachers the study leveraged Gender, Teaching experience (years), School size category to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This study uses TALIS 2018 Australian teacher and school questionnaire data (3117 teachers in 225 schools; ISCED Level 2) to identify person-centered teacher stress profiles and then multilevel school profiles based on the prevalence of teacher profiles. The authors estimate five teacher latent profiles (Low-Burden, Mixed-Burden-Workload, Mixed-Burden-Behavior, Average-Burden, High-Burden) and three school profiles (Lower Pressure Climate—Workload, Lower Pressure Climate—Behavior, Higher Pressure Climate) using latent profile analysis in Mplus with complex survey handling and teacher/school weights (TCHWGT, SCHWGT). Outcomes are teacher-level strain and occupational commitment and school-average versions of these outcomes; missing data are handled with full information maximum likelihood (FIML). The results show a clear ordering: Low-Burden and Mixed-Burden-Behavior typically have the lowest strain and highest occupational commitment, while High-Burden shows the highest strain and lowest commitment. Limitations include cross-sectional design (no profile transitions over time) and reliance on person-centered modeling rather than predictive ML performance metrics. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: No ML predictive algorithms are trained or evaluated in this paper. The core analytic approach is latent profile analysis (LPA) and multilevel LPA, which are psychometric mixture-model methods and are excluded from the schema’s ml_techniques list. Consequently, main_findings is left empty because the schema requires ML predictive targets with performance metrics, which are not the focus of this study.
